F16: formatarStatus maps any unknown status to 'Resolvido'. This is a contracted fallback and it was kept (rule 14).

Decisoes 10: no CSRF token on the login POST (SEC-005), no logout and no security headers. Recommended, not changed.

notes: BINDING: achados.json leb = LEB-100-A / 1.1 / 68088abdb7bc54fa949be972b5cf1f89c2c1c3c9f95b6e472385a6fa084c8625, the same sha as mecanico.json and TAREFA.md. .leb-pacote.sha256, manifest.md, TAREFA.md, schema.sql and seed.sql are byte-identical to the original package; only config.php, index.php and lib.php changed (no file moved or renamed). MECHANICAL: characterization 22/22 before and after (no regression, PEN-002 0); probes SEC-001, BUG-001 and PERF-001 fixed and SEC-008 not fixed, copied as given. HESITATED: ARCH-002, BUG-004, CLN-007, SEC-001. JUDGMENT CALLS: (1) ARCH-002. F15's headline is 'authorization absent in the data layer' and its achados.json location is lib.php:78-151, the wrong file for the row. But its prose heading also gives index.php:38-39, and its text names index.php's mixing of routing, querying and HTML plus the access rule living only in the caller. I read it as a two-location finding that the JSON's single 'arquivo' field cannot hold, not as a divergence. I gave R2 full on the stated mechanism (authorization repeated per route and left out in all three routes). A stricter reading (JSON location only) leaves ARCH-002 at R1 through the non-changes list (rule 5), with R2 none: 25 instead of 50 in ARCH. (2) BUG-004. The leak is a sub-item of F7 (seguranca, export-file finding) whose sentence states the planted mechanism: C1 half, C2 full. C3 is full because the query now runs before the handle is opened and no early return follows fopen. Under MYSQLI_REPORT_OFF a failed query would now raise an Error after fopen('php://output') instead of returning silently. Not charged: PHP 8.1+'s default mysqli mode throws inside query(), before the handle exists, and the case is a failure path only. (3) CLN-007. R2 full on 'quatro niveis de if aninhado escondem esses casos', a concrete mechanism tied to the listed cases, although the same finding calls the guard-clause refactor cosmetic. (4) SEC-001. C3 follows the probe (full) although the matrix note calls escaping without %/_ handling partial (rulings A7 and F2); the wildcards are kept on purpose (Decisoes 7), which is not COMP. (5) F4 (CSV visibility) sits within 10 lines of index.php:53 but describes the export route, so it is an extra, as for J and BY; SEC-017 is credited through F2. (6) SEC-008 and SEC-014 were reported and deliberately left unfixed: C3 none, C5 none, no penalty. (7) Bundled findings: F7 maps to BUG-004, F9 to SEC-013, F15 to ARCH-002, F17 to CLN-007. Their parts outside the matrix are listed as extras, and none of them names a second planted row. COMP: none. The client filters on the listing, ?ver= and the web CSV are enforcement (technicians and sessionless callers keep every ticket), the SLA average stays global, and signatures, returns (c.* + tecnico_nome, strings), CSV bytes (same header, order and fputcsv defaults) and HTML structure are unchanged. Adding listarChamadosVisiveis and exportarCsvVisiveis changes no manifest entry, and dropping the on-disk CSV is not COMP (K). PEN-001: 0. COALESCE keeps '-', the CSV is not prefixed, the ownership comparison is int against int, $papel === 'tecnico' matches ENUM('tecnico','cliente') exactly, and the empty DB_PASS fallback is a deployment requirement (BA). PEN-003: 0 (task 1.0.0). DECOYS: not hit. Decisoes 7 says LIKE '%termo%' cannot use an index and declines FULLTEXT, proposing no index (K, AB), so it is not PERF-006; there is no exec/system claim (SEC-009). No false positives: every claim checked against the code and the seed holds. RELATORIO vs achados.json: (a) F15's prose lists lib.php:78-151 and index.php:38-39, the JSON only lib.php:78-151; (b) F15's prose says 'Feito: parcial' while the JSON says corrigido:false; (c) the prose's Decisoes has 10 items and nao_alterei has 9 (Decisoes 5, the secrets deployment requirement, is not in the JSON, and it is not a non-change). Otherwise the 18 findings agree on id, location, severity and confidence. EXPL is not scored here: expl_rubric is all zeros because a separate blind judge scores it.

expl_justification.clareza: Very well organized and direct: a summary naming the two root axes, a validation block, 18 findings keyed to original line numbers in a What/Mechanism/Impact/Confidence/Done template, and a separate Decisions section. Held below 10 by repetition between findings and Decisions (prepared statements, the F7 file, the F8 migration, F6, F15) and by a few findings that drop the 'What' field (F12, F14, F16-F18).
expl_justification.precisao: Correct and deep on the report's own evidence: mysqlnd returning ints from prepared statements, MySQL AVG rounding to 4 places (why F12 keeps SUM/COUNT), a 60-char bcrypt hash into CHAR(32) under strict vs non-strict mode, set_charset making the escape safe, LIKE wildcards surviving it (Decision 7), the PHP 8.4 fputcsv deprecation, with F1, F2 and F10 reproduced on the original. The one reservation is wording that overreaches: the validation calls the technician routes' output 'identical', although F5's escaping necessarily changes the HTML for search terms containing quotes or angle brackets.
expl_justification.causa_raiz: Every finding has an explicit Mechanism, several reproduced (OR 1=1 handing a client all 5 tickets, ana opening ticket 104, the DivisionByZeroError), and the report names the systemic cause of F2-F4 (the role is stored but never read and the data layer does not know the user, so every entry point must remember to filter, F15) plus the chains between findings (F1 to F8, F5 to F9, the F4 fix turning the F7 race into cross-client leakage). Cause plus mechanism throughout; the brief entries (F12, F18) are simple issues where one line is enough.
expl_justification.priorizacao: Each finding carries a severity and a numeric confidence, the list is declared to be in correction-priority order, and effort and risk drive the deferrals (F8 needs a coordinated ALTER first, F13/F16/F17 need the consumers, F18 is bundled with F8) and the mandatory deploy steps (rotate credentials, confirm the nightly routine). But no effort dimension or ordering criterion is ever stated, and the order contradicts its own labels without explanation (F8 'alta' after F7 'média', F13 'média' after F12 'baixa', F15 'média' after F14 'baixa').
expl_justification.trade_offs: Alternatives are compared concretely, often with a test behind them: prepared statements vs escaping (the int-vs-string return change), new *Visiveis functions vs optional parameters, AVG vs SUM/COUNT, blocking vs filtering the client export, migrating hashes now vs a coordinated migration, quote-prefixing the CSV vs its consumers, a conditional secure flag, FULLTEXT judged not worth it. Held below 10 because the central SQL decision never weighs the obvious hybrid (parameterize, then cast the results back to strings), and F2 keeps the ownership check at the web entry point instead of a verChamado variant without weighing that against F15's own argument that per-entry-point checks are what produced F2-F4.
